claim: Let \(G\) be a finite connected simple bipartite graph with bipartition \(X\sqcup Y\), at least one edge, and no \(4\)-cycle. For every choice of roots \(r_y\in N_G(y)\) for \(y\in Y\), the \(X\)-component \(K_X\) of the Lovász neighborhood complex \(\mathcal N(G)\) simplicially collapses onto the graph \(T_X\) with vertex set \(X\) and edges \(\{r_y,x\}\) for \(x\in N_G(y)\setminus\{r_y\}\). Moreover \(T_X\) is exactly the graph obtained from \(G\) by contracting the forest \(\{yr_y:y\in Y\}\). The analogous statement holds with \(X\) and \(Y\) interchanged. Consequently each component has an explicit graph spine homotopy equivalent to \(G\); in particular, if \(G\) is \(d\)-regular with \(|X|=|Y|=n\), then each component is homotopy equivalent to \(\bigvee^{n(d-2)+1}S^1\).

claim_to_evidence.computations: The bundled checker exhaustively validates the collapse sequence for all 1501 connected labeled bipartite square-free graphs on at most six vertices.
critical_proof_steps: Bipartiteness splits the neighborhood complex by sides.
No 4-cycle implies every face with at least two vertices has a unique supporting common neighbor.
Descending-cardinality pairs are therefore legal elementary simplicial collapses.
The residual rooted-star union equals the contraction of the selected-edge forest.
claim_to_evidence.domain: Finite connected simple bipartite graphs with at least one edge and no 4-cycle; arbitrary choice of one root neighbor for every vertex on the opposite side.
claim_to_evidence.unproved_limits: The finite enumeration is not an infinite proof; no extension is asserted for graphs containing a 4-cycle.

correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly verifies definitions, quantifiers, collapse order, freeness, and the forest-contraction identification. Square-freeness is used exactly where needed to prevent a size-two-or-larger face from lying in two neighborhood simplices. The independent finite checker replays the claimed elementary-collapse condition on 1501 small labeled graphs, but the acceptance rests on the uniform proof rather than enumeration.

originality.rationale: The final claim is deliberately stronger than the known homotopy-type consequence: it gives an elementary simplicial collapse onto an explicit forest-contraction minor for every root choice. The closest square-free Hom-complex theorem covers abstract homotopy types but the inspected full text contains no collapse terminology or explicit rooted-spine model; Shukla's earlier neighborhood-complex results cover different graph classes. Semantic database searches returned no implication of the explicit-collapse statement.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a uniform constructive reduction of a potentially high-dimensional neighborhood complex to a linear-size graph spine, not merely a homotopy classification. The spine is an explicit minor of the original graph, immediately exposing fundamental group, homology, and regular-family wedge multiplicity, and the proof pinpoints 4-cycles as the obstruction to the simple local collapse scheme.
